column1: # OWASP ZAP rule tuning for Baseline + Full-Scan profiles.
# Spec: spec/nfr/NFR-015_OWASP-ZAP-Security-Scanning.md §6.1
# Format (tab-separated, exactly four fields):
#   <PluginID>
# Confidence ∈ {LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH} — POSITIONAL AND READ BY NOBODY. The column is
# kept so the file stays shaped like ZAP's own rule files, but neither `zap_gate.py`
# nor ZAP acts on it: `zap_common.load_config` unpacks it into a variable literally
# named `ignore` and keeps only the note after it. A suppression is bounded by its
# `scope=`, not by this value, and `40018 IGNORE LOW` suppresses a High-confidence
# instance exactly as `MEDIUM` does.
# THRESHOLD: **only IGNORE is honoured.** ZAP's own vocabulary is
# {PASS, IGNORE, INFO, WARN, FAIL} — note that "OFF", which an earlier version of
# this header listed, is not among them and makes `zap_common.load_config` raise
# `Level OFF is not a supported level`. But ZAP does not read this file at all
# (see below), and `zap_gate.py` implements no threshold overrides, so a WARN or
# FAIL row would change nothing. It is rejected with a message rather than
# accepted and left inert; the severity policy lives in `zap_gate.py` itself
# Tabs, not spaces: a space-separated row parses to a single field. `zap_gate.py`
# reports that with the file and line rather than skipping it, because the two
# are indistinguishable in a diff and the silent skip would leave the suppression
# not applied with nobody told.
# WHO READS THIS FILE: `scripts/security/zap_gate.py` alone, via `--rules`. It is
# deliberately NOT passed to the ZAP wrappers with `-c` (or `-u`), because
# `zap-api-scan.py` decides its active scan policy from whether that config
# produced any entries:
#     scan_policy = 'API-Minimal'
#     if config_dict:
#         scan_policy = 'Default Policy'
#         zap.ascan.enable_all_scanners(scanpolicyname=scan_policy)
# The first suppression would therefore swap a 23-rule minimal policy for the full
# active rule set — an unrelated, unbounded widening of a scan that runs under a
# 45-minute job timeout — and the only shape ZAP can express is "turn this rule
# off everywhere". The gate drops matching INSTANCES instead, so the rule keeps
# running and a genuine finding at another URL still blocks.
# Every IGNORE row MUST carry, in the Note column:
#   * `# expires YYYY-MM-DD — approved by <role> (YYYY-MM-DD)` — the expiry, the
#     approver, AND the date of that approval. Expired is a CI warning; after 30
#     days of grace it fails the build and stops applying, so the finding it was
#     covering reappears in the run that goes red. The approval date is not
#     decoration: it bounds the row's life at twelve months (366 days) WITHOUT a
#     clock, so the check means the same on every day and in every lane. Deriving
#     the span from "today" would put a calendar dependency into a required lane,
#     which is how a ZAP rule ends up blocking every merge in the repository.
#   * EXACTLY ONE `scope=<url regex>` — the URLs the suppression covers, matched
#     with `re.search` and therefore UNANCHORED: `scope=/api/v1/auth/` is a prefix
#     that also covers `/api/v1/auth/anything`, and `scope=/x/confirm` would cover
#     `/x/confirm-v2` too. Anchor it (`^…$` against the full URL) when that
#     matters. `scope=.*` means rule-wide and has to be written out; there is no
#     implicit rule-wide. Exactly one, because the note is prose and the first
#     match wins: a note that MENTIONS `scope=.*` while explaining why it did not
#     use it would silence the rule everywhere. Two candidates is rejected.
# `src/backend/tests/unit/guards/test_zap_rule_suppressions.py` enforces the file
# format and the absence of `-c`/`-u` in the workflows; `test_zap_gate.py` enforces
# what the gate does with a row. Both run in the REQUIRED `Write-route and tree
# guards` lane.
# This file is intentionally empty in Phase 1. Tuning entries are added
# alongside their motivating findings in Phase 3.
